text: A pipeline nobody can explain is genuinely a pipeline nobody else can safely maintain. In a real job, the person reviewing your work almost never has time to read every activity's configuration themselves. The five-minute walkthrough you can give is often the actual deliverable, as much as the pipeline itself.

The problem, in one sentence: Northwind's sales data was stuck on-premises, with no automated way to see it before the morning leadership meeting. Then the architecture at a glance — walk the five-stage diagram. And one deliberate design decision, genuinely explained — the Filter-before-Join ordering is a good candidate, because it's a real decision with a real reason, not an arbitrary default.

How it fails safely: the three-layer error handling — retry, log, alert — is exactly what separates a demo from something production-ready. And how you'd know if it broke: point at the Log Analytics query. I don't have to guess if this is reliable, I can query it — genuinely the strongest way to close that part of a walkthrough.

The strongest way to close the whole thing is a direct callback to the original four requirements: on-premises data, solved by the self-hosted IR. Cleaned up and totaled, solved by filter, join, aggregate. Every morning on its own, solved by the trigger and error handling. No exposed passwords, solved by Key Vault on both source and sink. Four asks, four real checkmarks.

Eleven chapters, fifty-eight lessons, and one finished, production-patterned pipeline: integration runtimes, pipelines and control flow, mapping data flows, every real trigger type, monitoring and error handling that actually holds up overnight, Fabric's re-imagined architecture, and a genuine CI slash CD story from a laptop to production. That's the real shape of the job — not just a tour of a feature list. Congratulations on finishing the Data Factory course.
